cse-2010-cs-33.approach: Draw the space–time diagram cycle by cycle. Two things delay instructions: the **single PO unit** (a structural hazard — MUL and DIV occupy it for 3 and 6 cycles) and **RAW dependences**, which operand forwarding resolves by feeding a result straight into the next PO cycle. Instructions stay in order: one waiting in a stage blocks those behind it.
cse-2010-cs-33.given:
Stages IF, ID, OF, PO, WO — 1 cycle each, except PO: ADD/SUB 1, MUL 3, DIV 6.

- $I_0$: MUL $R_2 \leftarrow R_0 \times R_1$
- $I_1$: DIV $R_5 \leftarrow R_3 / R_4$
- $I_2$: ADD $R_2 \leftarrow R_5 + R_2$ (needs $R_5$ from $I_1$, $R_2$ from $I_0$)
- $I_3$: SUB $R_5 \leftarrow R_2 - R_6$ (needs $R_2$ from $I_2$)

steps.title: I0 (MUL) flows through, holding PO for 3 cycles
steps.body: IF 1, ID 2, OF 3, PO 4–6, WO 7. Nothing is ahead of it, so it never waits.

steps.title: I1 (DIV) waits for the PO unit
steps.body: IF 2, ID 3, OF 4 — but PO is busy with MUL until the end of cycle 6. I1 stalls in OF during cycles 5–6, executes PO in **7–12** (6 cycles) and writes back in **13**.

steps.title: I2 (ADD) waits for $R_5$, forwarded at the end of cycle 12
steps.body: IF 3, ID 4; OF is occupied by I1 until cycle 6, so I2 enters OF in 7. Its operand $R_5$ is produced by DIV at the end of cycle 12 and **forwarded**, so I2's PO is cycle **13** and WO is **14**. ($R_2$ from MUL was ready long before.)

steps.title: I3 (SUB) gets $R_2$ forwarded from I2
steps.body: I3 is fetched in 4 but must queue behind I2: ID in 7, OF in 13 (after I2 leaves OF). $R_2$ comes out of I2's PO at the end of cycle 13 and is forwarded, so I3's PO is **14** and WO is **15**.

steps.title: Count the cycles
steps.body:
The last instruction completes WO in cycle 15, so the sequence takes **15 clock cycles**.

Check via the bottleneck: the PO unit is busy $3 + 6 + 1 + 1 = 11$ cycles back-to-back from cycle 4 (cycles 4–14), plus one WO cycle after it: $3 + 11 + 1 = 15$.

optionAnalysis.reason: 13 is when DIV writes back; ADD and SUB still need their PO and WO cycles after it.
PO is busy 4–14 without gaps thanks to forwarding; the final WO is in cycle 15.
17 is what you get **without** forwarding if a dependent instruction can fetch operands in the same cycle as the producer's write-back (OF of I2 in 13, OF of I3 in 15).
19 is the no-forwarding count when operands can be fetched only in the cycle **after** write-back.

cse-2010-cs-33.shortcut: With forwarding and in-order issue, the single PO unit is the bottleneck: first PO starts in cycle 4 (after IF, ID, OF), then PO runs $3+6+1+1 = 11$ cycles back to back, then one WO: $3 + 11 + 1 = 15$.
pitfalls: Letting DIV start PO in cycle 5 — the PO unit is still busy with MUL until cycle 6.
Waiting for WO before using a result: forwarding feeds it directly into the next PO cycle.
cse-2010-cs-33.verification: The diagram has PO occupied in exactly one instruction per cycle from 4 to 14 (MUL 4–6, DIV 7–12, ADD 13, SUB 14) and every dependent PO starts one cycle after its producer's last PO cycle.
